assessments.statement: Setting (1): for every SDDM positive-definite L, the nuclear Nystrom error of K = L^{-1} satisfies diminishing error-reduction on non-empty nested index sets: f(S u {i}) - f(S) <= f(T u {i}) - f(T) for all non-empty S subset of T, i not in T.
assessments.rationale: Supported only by experiments/sketches/notes — evidence, not verification.

assessments.statement: Setting (2): for every SDD positive-definite L (mixed-sign off-diagonals allowed), the nuclear Nystrom error of K = L^{-1} satisfies diminishing error-reduction on non-empty nested index sets.
assessments.rationale: Contradicted or refuted by recorded evidence.

assessments.statement: Candidate counterexample to setting (2): the 6x6 SDD positive-definite matrix L* with rows [8, 3/2, -1/4, -3/4, 1, -3/2], [3/2, 26/3, -3/2, -1/3, 4/3, 1], [-1/4, -3/2, 9/2, -1, -1/2, -1/4], [-3/4, -1/3, -1, 61/12, -3/2, 1/2], [1, 4/3, -1/2, -3/2, 28/3, -2], [-3/2, 1, -1/4, 1/2, -2, 33/4], with S={0}, T={0,3}, i=5, gives f(S u {i}) - f(S) = -207777829717/1469109624035 > -156716773/1107431115 = f(T u {i}) - f(T) in exact rational arithmetic, so the diminishing-error-reduction inequality fails on this instance. Independent confirmation of the general statement's failure still requires an external verification record.
assessments.rationale: Supported only by experiments/sketches/notes — evidence, not verification.
